title: Ownership and state capital in Chinese and Singaporean OSATs: JCET (China Resources), Tongfu (AMD JV), Huatian, WiseRoad/UTAC and their customer ties
why_it_matters: Three of the top-six OSATs are Chinese and grew double digits in 2024 with policy support; the largest (JCET) passed from the Big Fund and SMIC to state-owned China Resources in 2024, and Tongfu does most of AMD's back end through a JV. Ownership decides export-control exposure and customer risk.
questions: Who controls each large Chinese OSAT (JCET, Tongfu, Huatian, WiseRoad) and what stakes do the Big Fund, local governments and chip companies hold?
What share of AMD's back end runs through the Tongfu ATMP JVs, and what did AMD buy from them by year?
Which Western chip companies depend on Chinese-owned back-end plants in Malaysia and Singapore?
primary_sources: AMD Form 10-K related-party note on the ATMP JVs

title: Americas back-end build-out: US CHIPS ITSI Fund partner countries (Costa Rica, Panama, Mexico) and US advanced packaging plants (Amkor Arizona, SK hynix Indiana, Intel New Mexico)
why_it_matters: SIA/BCG expect back-end capacity to spread to Latin America and the US is funding it through the US$500m ITSI Fund, but Intel is closing its Costa Rica assembly/test site by end-2026 and US packaging plants will not produce before 2028. Whether an Americas back end materialises is unclear.
questions: What ATP capacity exists and is planned in Mexico, Costa Rica and Panama, and what has ITSI funded?
What are the status, capacity and customers of US advanced packaging plants (Amkor Peoria, SK hynix West Lafayette, Intel Rio Rancho)?
What is North America's share of ATP capacity today versus the 3% cited in 2022?
primary_sources: US State Department ITSI Fund announcements
